rated_messages.input_message: Think about what is really important to you. Maybe it's spending time with family or a friend, exercising, doing something spiritual, or creating something. Whatever it is, take a step in that direction.
Instead of lighting up a cigarette, light a scented candle or burn some incense.
Acknowledge your unhelpful thought by writing it down on a piece of paper. Then let it be on it's way by crumpling it up and tossing it in a trash can.

Imagine walking into a social situation in three months' time as a non-smoker. Now hold that picture and imagine you're that person now. Seeing yourself as a non-smoker now can make it much easier to resist!
If you get urges, remind yourself that cigarettes did that to you. If you go back to them, they will keep making you suffer. Now you are breaking free.
If you usually smoke while you talk on the phone, try taking the next call in a place where you can't smoke and focus on the conversation. The urge will pass.
Stop! Breathe. What is going on around you? Inside you? Allow everything to be just as it is. Breathe again.
Try to stop smoking by setting yourself a rule. For example, "IF I am tempted, THEN I will chew on some mints" - make your own rule that will work for you.
When your mind tells you that you will be less stressed after smoking a cigarette, remember that you don't have to listen to that thought. It's just a thought and nothing more.
Instead of smoking, keep your fingers busy by scrolling through your phone.
